summary: This work demonstrates breakeven quantum error correction with five distinct high-rate qLDPC codes on a 40-ion $^{133}$Ba trapped-ion system, achieving logical error rates $9\times$ better than prior superconducting demonstrations and logical qubit lifetimes comparable to physical qubits ($3.95 \pm 0.68$ s vs. $3.84 \pm 0.48$ s). The key innovation is a full implementation of the optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture enabling mid-circuit measurement without ion transport or dedicated coolant ions, providing sufficient flexibility to implement three code families (qLDPC, topological, concatenated) with different connectivity requirements on a single device without reconfiguration.
motivation: qLDPC codes promise higher encoding rates than surface codes but are notoriously difficult to implement due to non-local two-qubit gate connectivity requirements; previous demonstrations required hardware specifically engineered for a single code instance.
method: All-to-all steerable Raman beams address any ion pair in a stationary chain without transport. The OMG architecture uses phase-coherent shuttling within a single ion between the ground $6^2S_{1/2}$ and metastable $5^2D_{5/2}$ manifolds to enable parallel mid-circuit measurement and reset of up to 16 ancillae simultaneously while sympathetically cooling the chain, eliminating the need for dedicated coolant species.
result: For the BB5 $[[18,4,3]]$ code: $p_L = 1.95 \pm 0.39 \times 10^{-2}$ (X basis) and $1.10 \pm 0.15 \times 10^{-2}$ (Z basis) per cycle per qubit, giving $T_X = 1.06 \pm 0.18$ s and $T_Z = 1.90 \pm 0.23$ s. The GB5 $[[26,2,5]]$ code achieved $T_{\mathcal{N}} = 3.95 \pm 0.68$ s, exceeding the physical lifetime by under 3% accounting for error bars.
